rated_messages.input_message: Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
Try chewing gum if you have trouble resisting smoking when other people light up around you.
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
Urges are like annoying ads. You might see them but you don't have to buy what they're selling.

Remind yourself that by staying quit, you'll be freeing yourself from the constant cycle of cigarette, nicotine withdrawal, feeling stressed as a result and wanting another cigarette. Keep going and this will be a thing of the past!
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.
Life can get you really stressed out, but turning to cigs isn't the answer. Call or text family and friends instead. Ask them to help you stay on track.
